static_findings.snippet: - **Force required**: Use `--force` to remove worktrees with uncommitted changes
- Prunable worktree -> Directory was deleted manually, run `git worktree prune`
- **Cleanup regularly**: Remove worktrees for merged branches to avoid clutter

content.user_title: Manage Git Worktrees for Parallel Development
content.value_statement: Parallel branch work can disrupt local changes and slow urgent fixes. This skill guides Git worktree creation, status checks, and cleanup for isolated development.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Git worktrees instead of switching branches.
Generates worktree plans for existing branches and new branches.
Lists active worktrees and explains clean, dirty, detached, or prunable states.
Plans cleanup for merged or stale worktrees with confirmation steps.
Supports isolated hotfix and pull request review workflows.
limitations: Requires a Git repository that supports worktree commands.
Cannot guarantee branch names or paths are safe without user review.
Does not replace repository backups or CI validation.
Force removal can discard uncommitted changes if used incorrectly.

use_cases.title: Parallel Feature Work
use_cases.description: Create a separate worktree for a second feature while current changes stay untouched.

use_cases.title: Emergency Hotfix Isolation
use_cases.description: Start a clean hotfix worktree from the main branch without disrupting active feature work.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Review Sandbox
use_cases.description: Review a pull request in its own worktree, then remove the workspace after testing.

prompt_templates.title: List Active Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my current Git worktrees, explain each status, and identify which one I am using.

prompt_templates.title: Create Feature Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree plan for branch feature/auth while preserving my current changes. Use a sibling worktrees directory.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Merged Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my worktrees, identify merged branches, and present a cleanup plan that asks before any removal.

prompt_templates.title: Design Parallel Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a worktree workflow for two features, one hotfix, and a pull request review. Include naming, paths, and cleanup rules.

output: A numbered list of active worktrees with path, branch, commit, and clean or dirty state.
A short recommendation for cleanup or saving changes.

output_examples.input: I need a hotfix without disturbing current work.
output_examples.output: A hotfix branch and sibling worktree plan, with next steps for fixing, committing, and removing the temporary workspace.
A dry-run cleanup plan that lists candidates, warns about uncommitted changes, and asks for confirmation before removal.

best_practices: Review generated paths before creating or removing worktrees.
Check for uncommitted changes before cleanup.
Use clear branch slugs so worktree directories stay predictable.
anti_patterns: Using force removal before saving or committing work.
Creating worktrees inside the main repository directory.
Keeping stale worktrees after branches are merged.

faq.question: What does this skill help me manage?
faq.answer: It helps plan Git worktree creation, listing, status review, and cleanup for parallel development.

faq.question: Does it replace normal Git commands?
faq.answer: No. It guides command selection and workflow decisions while you remain responsible for execution.

faq.question: Can it help with urgent hotfixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan an isolated hotfix worktree so current feature work stays untouched.

faq.question: Can it clean up old worktrees?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify cleanup candidates and present a confirmation-based removal plan.

faq.question: What should I check before removing a worktree?
faq.answer: Check branch status, uncommitted changes, merge state, and the exact path that will be removed.
